metadata.title: A motivated exposition of the proof of Tverberg's theorem
metadata.authors: V. Retinskiy, A. Ryabichev, A. Skopenkov

nodes.name: Convex hull
nodes.statement: The convex hull of a finite set of points $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in\mathbb{R}^d$ is $\langle p_1,\ldots,p_n\rangle := \{\alpha_1 p_1 + \ldots + \alpha_n p_n : \alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n \geq 0,\ \alpha_1+\ldots+\alpha_n = 1\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Convex hull as the set of convex combinations of finitely many points.

nodes.name: Radon's Theorem
nodes.statement: For every $d$, any $d+2$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be split into two sets whose convex hulls intersect.
nodes.statement_clean: Any d+2 points in R^d split into two groups with intersecting convex hulls.
conclusions: There exist $A_1 \sqcup A_2 = [d+2]$ such that $\langle p_i : i \in A_1\rangle \cap \langle p_i : i \in A_2\rangle \neq \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Tverberg's Theorem
nodes.statement: For every integers $d,r$ any $(d+1)(r-1)+1$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ can be decomposed into $r$ groups such that all the $r$ convex hulls of the groups have a common point.
nodes.statement_clean: Any (d+1)(r-1)+1 points in R^d partition into r groups whose convex hulls share a common point.
conclusions: There exists a partition $[(d+1)(r-1)+1] = A_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup A_r$ such that $\bigcap_{j=1}^{r} \langle p_i : i \in A_j \rangle \neq \emptyset$.

nodes.name: Barany's Colorful Caratheodory Theorem
nodes.statement: Let the point $0 \in \mathbb{R}^n$ lie in the convex hull of each of $n+1$ finite sets $M_1, M_2, \ldots, M_{n+1} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. Then there exist points $m_i \in M_i$ such that $0 \in \langle m_1, m_2, \ldots, m_{n+1}\rangle$.
nodes.statement_clean: If 0 is in the convex hull of each of n+1 finite sets in R^n, then a transversal exists whose convex hull also contains 0.
nodes.origin_citation: Barany 1982; Matousek, Lectures on Discrete Geometry, Sec. 8.2

nodes.name: Two-set partition equality
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i\in A_1} \alpha_i p_i = \sum_{i\in A_2} \alpha_i p_i$ and $\sum_{i\in A_1}\alpha_i = \sum_{i\in A_2}\alpha_i$, with $\sum_{i\in A_1}\alpha_i = 1$.

nodes.name: Lifted-vector reformulation
nodes.statement: Setting $p_i^+ := (p_i, 1) \in \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ and $S_j^+ := \sum_{i\in A_j}\alpha_i p_i^+$, the two equalities (1) are equivalent to a single equation $S_1^+ = S_2^+$.

nodes.name: Three-set partition equality (r=3)
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i\in A_1}\alpha_i p_i = \sum_{i\in A_2}\alpha_i p_i = \sum_{i\in A_3}\alpha_i p_i$ and $\sum_{i\in A_1}\alpha_i = \sum_{i\in A_2}\alpha_i = \sum_{i\in A_3}\alpha_i$, with $\sum_{i=1}^{2d+3}\alpha_i = 1$.

nodes.name: Vectors $\varphi_{j,i}$ in $\mathbb{R}^{2d+2}$
nodes.statement: $\varphi_{1,i} = (p_i^+, 0) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d+2}$,  $\varphi_{2,i} = (0, p_i^+) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d+2}$,  $\varphi_{3,i} = (-p_i^+, -p_i^+) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d+2}$.

nodes.name: Single-equation form (2)
nodes.statement: $\sum_{i\in A_1}\alpha_i \varphi_{1,i} + \sum_{i\in A_2}\alpha_i \varphi_{2,i} + \sum_{i\in A_3}\alpha_i \varphi_{3,i} = 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Radon's Theorem
nodes.statement: Lift points to $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ via $p_i^+ = (p_i,1)$; linear dependence of the $d+2$ lifted points yields coefficients $\mu_i$, and partitioning by sign gives the required decomposition.

nodes.name: Proof of Tverberg's Theorem (case $r=3$)
nodes.statement: Reduce the partition problem to a single vector equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2d+2}$ via auxiliary vectors $\varphi_{j,i}$, then apply the Colorful Caratheodory (Barany) Theorem.

nodes.name: Reformulate Radon as system (1)
nodes.statement: It suffices to find a partition $[d+2] = A_1 \sqcup A_2$ and nonnegative reals $\alpha_i$ satisfying $\sum_{A_1}\alpha_i p_i = \sum_{A_2}\alpha_i p_i$ and $\sum_{A_1}\alpha_i = \sum_{A_2}\alpha_i$, with $\sum_{A_1}\alpha_i = 1$ (replaceable by nonzero).

nodes.name: Lift to $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$
nodes.statement: Set $p_i^+ := (p_i,1) \in \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ and $S_j^+ := \sum_{i\in A_j}\alpha_i p_i^+$; the two equalities (1) become a single equation $S_1^+ = S_2^+$.

nodes.name: Use linear dependence in $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$
nodes.statement: The $d+2$ lifted points $p_i^+ \in \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ are linearly dependent, so there exist $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_{d+2}$ not all zero with $\sum_{i=1}^{d+2}\mu_i p_i^+ = 0$.

nodes.name: Split by sign of $\mu_i$
nodes.statement: Move negative-$\mu_i$ terms to the other side; the partition $A_1 = \{i : \mu_i \geq 0\}$, $A_2 = \{i : \mu_i < 0\}$ with $\alpha_i = |\mu_i|$ yields the required decomposition.

nodes.name: Reformulate Tverberg as system (1') for $r=3$
nodes.statement: For $r=3$ on $2d+3$ points, it suffices to find a partition $[2d+3] = A_1 \sqcup A_2 \sqcup A_3$ and $\alpha_i \geq 0$ with the three group-sums of $\alpha_i p_i$ equal and the three group-sums of $\alpha_i$ equal, with $\sum_{i=1}^{2d+3}\alpha_i = 1$.

nodes.name: Lift to $\mathbb{R}^{d+1}$
nodes.statement: Set $p_i^+ := (p_i,1) \in \mathbb{R}^{d+1}$ and $S_j^+ := \sum_{i\in A_j}\alpha_i p_i^+$; then (1') is equivalent to $S_1^+ = S_2^+ = S_3^+$.

nodes.name: Rewrite three equalities as a single vector equation
Introduce vectors $\varphi_{j,i}$
nodes.statement: Define $\varphi_{1,i} = (p_i^+, 0)$, $\varphi_{2,i} = (0, p_i^+)$, $\varphi_{3,i} = (-p_i^+, -p_i^+) \in \mathbb{R}^{2d+2}$; then $S_1^+ = S_2^+ = S_3^+ \iff \sum_{A_1}\alpha_i\varphi_{1,i} + \sum_{A_2}\alpha_i\varphi_{2,i} + \sum_{A_3}\alpha_i\varphi_{3,i} = 0$ (equation (2)).

nodes.name: Verify $0$ in convex hull of each $M_i$
nodes.statement: Since $0 = \frac{\varphi_{1,i} + \varphi_{2,i} + \varphi_{3,i}}{3} \in \langle \varphi_{1,i}, \varphi_{2,i}, \varphi_{3,i}\rangle$, the hypothesis of the Colorful Caratheodory Theorem holds for $n = 2d+2$ and $M_i = \{\varphi_{1,i}, \varphi_{2,i}, \varphi_{3,i}\}$.

nodes.name: Apply Barany's theorem and recover the partition
nodes.statement: Barany's theorem produces $m_i \in M_i$ with $0 \in \langle m_1,\ldots,m_{n+1}\rangle$. Define $A_j := \{i \in [2d+3] : m_i = \varphi_{j,i}\}$ for $j=1,2,3$; then there exist $\alpha_i \geq 0$ satisfying (2) and $\sum_i \alpha_i = 1$, completing the proof.

nodes.name: General-$r$ case analogous to $r=3$
nodes.statement: The proof is presented for $r=3$; the general case follows by the same argument (lifting, rewriting $r-1$ equalities as one vector equation in higher dimension, and applying the Colorful Caratheodory Theorem).

nodes.name: Radon as the case $r=2$
nodes.statement: Radon's theorem is the special case $r=2$ of Tverberg's theorem.
